$comment: T1.1-22: each process rule that crates/purlis-core/src/sandbox/seatbelt.rs writes (the floor's `FLOOR_PROCESSES`, one shape per bare deny, program and service, and the base's allows of signals and process info), and the escapes of escapes.json (ticket 22's) whose cells are aimed at it. `every_process_deny_rule_has_an_escape_cell` reads the source, so a new process rule fails the test until it is listed here; a rule with no cell aimed at it is listed under `debt`, with why, and leaves the list when its cell lands (`partial`: its escape has cells, aimed at another rule, so the escape's cover does not retire it). Linux's rules (crates/linux-sandbox) and the keys sandbox/claude.rs writes are not enumerated yet: see the pull request.

rules.what: the rule just inside which a signal to the chat's own child works, and just outside which one to a process outside is refused

debt.why: E-PROC-05's cell runs launchctl only: crontab exits 1 with no crontab even where it runs, so a command that is true only when it ran needs its own design
as crontab: at fails without atrun where it runs, so a refusal cannot be told from it by the exit status

debt.what: inspecting a process of the chat's own sandbox
debt.why: no cell inspects a process outside (proc_pidinfo of a planted process) yet: E-PROC-01 signals only
